To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following factors influence syllable structure in a typological and developmental perspective: 1. the number of syllable types, 2. the number of consonant types and 3. the sonority distance between syllable margins (cf. table 1).

(a) the acquisition of syllable structure proceeds in the following order: (i) the acquisition of sonorant consonants, which is the first step; (ii) the acquisition of obstruents; and (iii) the acquisition of the syllable coda, (b) the acquisition of vowel length and stress are closely related and proceed in tandem, and (c) the acquisition of stress proceeds in a stepwise fashion, from the rightmost syllable to the left.

(1) the acquisition of syllable structure proceeds in a step-wise fashion, with the first step consisting of the acquisition of the syllable structure of the language (the inventory of syllables) and the second step consisting of the learning of how these syllables can be combined in a word.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we account for the cross-linguistic variation in syllable structure?
the question how the acquisition of the correct ranking of constraints can be explained.
the acquisition of the rankings of the constraints of a particular language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OT model of language acquisition is not yet fully worked out, but that the model is promising and that it is a step towards an adequate theory.

the acquisition of the language-specific ranking of constraints is the result of a series of re-rankings, in which structural constraints are gradually demoted, or faithfulness constraints gradually promoted.
the OT approach to acquisition is not a theory of acquisition but a theory of the acquisition of a particular grammar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in how a learner acquires the ranking of constraints in the language he is exposed to.
we have shown how to derive the typological and developmental facts in a principled way, and we have done so in a unified framework.
the learner starts with a grammar with a structural bias, and that this grammar is gradually refined by promoting faithfulness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acquisition of the syllable types in a language can be modeled as an acquisition process of the ranking of the constraints in the OT grammar.
there are two ways to promote faithfulness: either by demoting structural constraint(s) or by promoting faithfulness.
there are many different ways to acquire a particular ranking.
